concepts.name: Threat model and attacker goals
concepts.summary: Recall that web apps are attacked through user-controlled input and name common goals such as data theft, account takeover and defacement.

concepts.name: Never trust client input
concepts.summary: Explain why every value in requests, including headers, cookies and hidden fields, can be forged by an attacker.

concepts.name: SQL injection basics
concepts.summary: Explain how concatenating user input into a SQL string lets an attacker change the query's meaning.

concepts.name: Cross-site scripting basics
concepts.summary: Explain how unescaped user content rendered in a page can run attacker JavaScript in a victim's browser.

concepts.name: Authentication versus authorization
aliases: who you are vs what you may do
concepts.summary: Distinguish verifying identity from deciding what an identified user may access.

concepts.name: Cross-site request forgery basics
concepts.summary: Explain how a malicious site can make a logged-in user's browser send unwanted requests because cookies are attached automatically.

concepts.name: HTTPS and password hygiene
concepts.summary: Recall that HTTPS protects data in transit and that passwords must never be stored in plain text.

misconceptions.text: Client-side JavaScript validation is enough to keep malicious input out.
Using HTTPS means the application itself is secure against injection and XSS.
Only large or famous sites are attacked, so small apps need little security.

concepts.name: Parameterized queries
concepts.summary: Apply parameterized queries so user data is sent separately from SQL code.

concepts.name: Stored, reflected and DOM XSS
concepts.summary: Distinguish the three XSS types by where the payload is stored and where it is injected.

concepts.name: Context-aware output encoding
concepts.summary: Apply the correct encoding for HTML body, attribute, URL and JavaScript contexts when rendering user data.

concepts.name: Secure password hashing
concepts.summary: Store passwords using a slow, salted hash designed for passwords rather than a fast general hash.

concepts.name: Session cookie flags
concepts.summary: Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite on session cookies and explain what each prevents.

concepts.name: CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies
concepts.summary: Apply synchronizer tokens and the SameSite cookie attribute to block forged cross-site requests.

concepts.name: Server-side access checks
concepts.summary: Check on the server that the current user may access each requested object, rather than hiding links.

misconceptions.text: Escaping quotes in user input is a reliable fix for SQL injection.
HTML-escaping output once is enough for every place the data is later used.
Hashing passwords with plain SHA-256 is secure enough.

concepts.name: Content Security Policy design
concepts.summary: Analyse an application's resource needs to build a CSP that limits script execution and reduces XSS impact.

concepts.name: Session management flaws
concepts.summary: Analyse session handling for fixation, weak IDs, missing rotation after login and poor expiry or logout.

concepts.name: Security misconfiguration review
concepts.summary: Find and fix default credentials, verbose errors, exposed admin interfaces and missing security headers.

concepts.name: Broken access control analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse endpoints for horizontal and vertical privilege escalation and missing function-level checks.

concepts.name: Server-side request forgery
concepts.summary: Analyse how user-supplied URLs make the server reach internal resources and apply allow-list defenses.

concepts.name: Other injection classes
concepts.summary: Recognise and prevent OS command, NoSQL, LDAP and template injection using the same separation of code and data.

concepts.name: Secure file upload handling
concepts.summary: Validate upload type, size and name, store files outside the web root and prevent path traversal.

concepts.name: Dependency vulnerability management
concepts.summary: Track and update third-party libraries using scanners and lock files to avoid known vulnerabilities.

misconceptions.text: A CSP makes output encoding unnecessary.
Using an ORM or framework makes an app immune to injection.
Checking a file's extension or Content-Type header is enough to make uploads safe.

concepts.name: Threat modelling web applications
concepts.summary: Decompose an application into trust boundaries and data flows to systematically identify threats.

concepts.name: Authentication architecture evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate login designs including MFA, OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect flows, reset flows and credential stuffing defenses.

concepts.name: Token security trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge cookie sessions versus bearer tokens, including storage risks, revocation and signature validation errors.

concepts.name: Same-origin policy and CORS
concepts.summary: Analyse how same-origin policy and CORS configuration can expose or protect data and where misconfiguration leaks.

concepts.name: Business logic and race flaws
concepts.summary: Analyse workflows for abuse such as price tampering, skipped steps and race conditions that scanners miss.

concepts.name: Security testing strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate the strengths and gaps of code review, static analysis, dynamic scanning and manual testing for a given app.

concepts.name: Deserialization and XXE risks
concepts.summary: Analyse how untrusted serialized data and XML parsers can lead to code execution or file disclosure.

misconceptions.text: A JWT is secure simply because it is signed, so its claims and algorithm need no further checks.
CORS protects a server from requests sent by other sites.
Passing an automated scanner means the application is secure.

concepts.name: Secure-by-design architecture
concepts.summary: Design application architecture with layered controls, least privilege and secure defaults that make whole bug classes hard to introduce.

concepts.name: Security guardrails in frameworks
concepts.summary: Create safe-by-default APIs and templates, such as auto-escaping and typed query builders, that remove the need for per-developer vigilance.

concepts.name: Risk-based vulnerability prioritisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate findings by exploitability, exposure and business impact to decide what to fix first and what risk to accept.

concepts.name: Advanced browser attack chaining
concepts.summary: Evaluate how seemingly minor flaws such as sanitizer bypass, open redirects and cache poisoning combine into serious exploits.

concepts.name: Secure SDLC and DevSecOps programme
concepts.summary: Design a development lifecycle integrating threat modelling, automated checks, review gates and secrets management.

concepts.name: Incident detection and response
concepts.summary: Evaluate logging, anomaly detection and WAF strategy and plan response to web application compromises.

concepts.name: Security standards and assurance
concepts.summary: Evaluate an application against standards like OWASP ASVS and use them to set verifiable requirements.

misconceptions.text: A web application firewall can substitute for fixing vulnerable code.
Every high-severity CVSS finding must be fixed before any lower-scored one regardless of context.
Moving security checks to a final pre-release audit is as effective as integrating them throughout development.
